changes: MemberExecutionSetup binds installation, serial source initialization, DNS initialization and native authority ports to original stage requests and predecessor receipts.

run_execution_round holds the existing exclusive round journal lock through setup, native operations and unified cleanup; all infrastructure is explicit and no default live transport or credential discovery is added.

Completed setup replies can be read back, but an uncertain mutation cannot be replayed. Recovery stops authority first and requires every interface to reconcile before exact cleanup pins are collected.
Only allowlisted safe receipts and cleanup fields enter the journal. Changed original requests, foreign roles, duplicate pins, unprojected private fields and changed recovery receipts are rejected.
MemberInstallation uses the existing verified runtime extractor for real filesystem installation checks and exclusive private-file imports. Hash, owner, link and mode validation precede publication.

Linux testing found that a restrictive umask left the installation root untraversable by the service user. Verified runtime installation now explicitly grants 0711 traversal; private directories remain 0700 and private files 0600.
The unarmed runtime packaging inventory includes the new modules and their complete Linux test dependencies. No new full runtime or node release was frozen.
real_checks: Actual Linux file locks, SIGKILL/SIGTERM, on-disk recovery and once-only mutations through both assembled and newly bound execution entries.
Real runtime extraction with synthetic archive inputs, public PHP loading by a separate unprivileged service user, private-file denial, symlink/hash/permission drift rejection.
Real loopback HTTP POST to the existing MachineProvisionController and MachineProvisionService with a minimal disposable application container.
MySQL 8.4 InnoDB persistence across HTTP process restart, duplicate receipt idempotency and unchanged sibling task.
Wrong bearer token, mismatched installation identity, unexpected fields, oversized requests, expired task and disabled callback gate rejection.
A real Redis account lock held in the parent process produces HTTP 503 without updating the task; a later callback succeeds after release.
Conflicting callbacks return HTTP 409 without overwriting success.
A synthetic missing-column failure after the task update proves the real MySQL transaction rolls back; schema restoration permits a subsequent successful callback.

isolation.network: MySQL and Redis share a network=none Docker namespace; tests enter that namespace; no external IPv4/IPv6 routes or published host ports
isolation.mysql_privileges: dedicated database-only user; no global grants or SUPER privilege
isolation.service_credentials: synthetic fixture-only values; no real cloud, DNS, SSH or panel credentials
isolation.http: 127.0.0.1 random port; exact test URI; no redirects
isolation.queues: callback dispatcher is NullQueue; no Horizon or queue worker is started; only disposable fixture configuration is used
isolation.dependencies: locked Composer install before namespace entry, scripts/plugins disabled

attempts.cause: Real service-user loading exposed a 0700 installation root after umask filtering.
Rollback fixture attempted a trigger requiring extra MySQL privilege; switched to reversible column-rename fault injection without broadening database privileges.

limitations: Setup and recovery infrastructure ports are simulated. This verifies explicit bindings and real local installation primitives, not a completed remote bootstrap or a live R35 run.
HTTP tests invoke the real receipt controller/service over TCP with a minimal application container, not production Nginx/TLS or the complete application middleware stack.
Installation permission tests use synthetic archives and PHP payloads. They do not prove the whole frozen application starts under the eventual service configuration.
Real cloud capacity, actual agent installations/continuous reports, wall-clock cooldown, SSH authorization and external DNS propagation remain unverified.
New complete LF runtime freeze, scoped read-only preflight and renewed execution authority remain necessary. This evidence is not permission to deploy, create machines or execute R34.
